In this vignette we try to predict the arrival delay of flights from New York
using weather data at the departure airport. We use the `ridgereg()` function
from this package and choose lambda with a validation set.

## Packages
```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(Lab4PKG)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(caret)
```


## Data

Flights dataset has `r nrow(nycflights13::flights)` observations (rows) and `r ncol(nycflights13::flights)` features (columns).\
Weather dataset has `r nrow(nycflights13::weather)` observations (rows) and `r ncol(nycflights13::weather)` features (columns).


```{r}
cat("Columns in flights:", paste(colnames(nycflights13::flights), collapse = ", "), "\n\n")
cat("Columns in weather:", paste(colnames(nycflights13::weather), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

Plan: from the weather data we take time_hour, wind_speed, wind_dir, wind_gust
and visib. From the flights data we take time_hour, arr_delay and origin, and
match the two on origin and time.

### Filter weather data
```{r}
weather_filtered <- nycflights13::weather |> 
  select("origin", "time_hour", "wind_speed", "wind_dir", "wind_gust", "visib")
weather_filtered
```


### Filter flights data
```{r}
flights_filtered <- nycflights13::flights |> 
  select("origin", "time_hour", "arr_delay")
flights_filtered
```

### Join both datasets
```{r}
flights_weather <- left_join(flights_filtered, weather_filtered, by = c("origin", "time_hour"))
flights_weather
```


## Cleaning the data

```{r}
knitr::kable(t(colSums(is.na(flights_weather))), caption = "Missing values per column")
```

wind_gust is removed since about 3/4 of its values are missing. The remaining
rows with missing values are removed.

The wind_dir column gives wind direction in degrees. 10° and 350° are pretty
close to each other, but as numbers they are far apart, so the model would not
see them as similar.

To solve this we use the unit circle and split wind_dir into an x and a y value.

```{r}
delay_dataset <- flights_weather |> 
  mutate(wind_x = cos(wind_dir * pi / 180),
         wind_y = sin(wind_dir * pi / 180),
         wind_dir = NULL) |> 
  select(!c("origin", "time_hour", "wind_gust")) |> 
  drop_na()

cat("Rows before cleaning:", nrow(flights_weather), "\n")
cat("Rows after cleaning:", nrow(delay_dataset), "\n")
delay_dataset
```


## Splitting the data
The data is split into 80% training, 15% validation and 5% test data.

```{r}
set.seed(67)
train_idx <- createDataPartition(delay_dataset$arr_delay, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_data <- delay_dataset[train_idx, ]
rest_data <- delay_dataset[-train_idx, ]

validation_idx <- createDataPartition(rest_data$arr_delay, p = 0.75, list = FALSE)
validation_data <- rest_data[validation_idx, ]
test_data <- rest_data[-validation_idx, ]
```

```{r}
cat("Training:  ", round(nrow(train_data) / nrow(delay_dataset), 3), "\n")
cat("Validation:", round(nrow(validation_data) / nrow(delay_dataset), 3), "\n")
cat("Test:      ", round(nrow(test_data) / nrow(delay_dataset), 3), "\n")
```


## Model

We add interactions between wind speed and the two wind direction values
(wind_x and wind_y). The idea is that wind direction should not matter much
when it is calm, but when the wind is strong, the direction can make a big
difference, for example if it blows straight against the runway or from the
side. In other words, the effect of the direction depends on the speed.

Multiplying the speed with wind_x and wind_y gives the wind's strength in the
east-west and north-south direction.

### Root mean squared error (RMSE)
```{r}
rmse <- function(error) return(sqrt(mean(error^2)))
```


### Evaluate different lambda values
Each lambda is trained on the training data and evaluated on the validation data.

```{r}
lambdas <- 10^seq(-2, 6, by = 1)
total_error <- numeric(length(lambdas))
form <- formula(arr_delay ~ wind_speed + visib + wind_x + wind_y + wind_speed:wind_x + wind_speed:wind_y)

for (i in seq_along(lambdas)) {
  mod <- ridgereg$new(formula = form, data = train_data, lambda = lambdas[i])
  pred <- mod$predict(newdata = validation_data)
  error <- validation_data$arr_delay - pred
  total_error[i] <- rmse(error)
}

knitr::kable(data.frame(lambda = lambdas, rmse = total_error), 
             col.names =c("Lambda","Root Mean Squared Error"),
             digits = 3)
```


### Find best lambda value
```{r}
min_error_idx <- which.min(total_error)
best_lambda <- lambdas[min_error_idx]
cat("Best lambda:", best_lambda, "\n")
cat("Validation RMSE:", round(total_error[min_error_idx], 2), "minutes\n")
```


## Test
The model with the best lambda is evaluated once on the test data.

```{r}
test_mod <- ridgereg$new(formula = form, data = train_data, lambda = best_lambda)
test_pred <- test_mod$predict(test_data)
test_error <- test_data$arr_delay - test_pred
test_rmse <- rmse(test_error)
cat("Test RMSE:", round(test_rmse, 2), "minutes\n")
```


## Conclusion
The best lambda on the validation data was `r best_lambda`, and the model got
a test RMSE of `r round(test_rmse, 2)` minutes.

The choice of lambda had almost no effect. The validation RMSE barely changed
between the different values. A likely reason is that we have a lot of data and only a few features, 
so the model has little room to overfit and ridge has little to correct.

The error is large, which shows that the weather variables only explain a small
part of the delays. One reason is that the weather data only describes the
conditions at the departure airport. Weather at the destination, and other
causes such as air traffic or technical problems, are not included.
